claims.text: At stage-2, Order's public constructor throws ArgumentException when the items list is empty or when any item has Quantity < 1, then sets CustomerId, Items, PlacedAt and Status = "new".
The constructor assigns the items parameter directly (Items = items) without copying, so the caller's variable and order.Items refer to the same List<OrderItem>; clearing either empties both.
claims.source_hint: C# reference: reference types (assignment copies the reference); examples/don-hang @ stage-2: DonHang.Domain/Entities.cs:67

claims.text: Items is declared public List<OrderItem> Items { get; private set; } = []; a private setter only stops outside code assigning the property, while the getter returns the list object itself.
claims.source_hint: C# programming guide: Properties / Restricting accessor accessibility; Entities.cs:36 @ stage-2

claims.text: List<T> has public Clear(), Remove and Add methods that change the list in place.
At stage-2 OrderItem has public get/set for OrderId, ProductId, Quantity and UnitPriceVnd, and Order has no method that is called when an item's Quantity or the Items list changes.

At stage-2 neither create endpoint (OrdersController.Create, OrdersV2Controller.Create) changes the list after passing it to PlaceOrderAsync; OrderService sets IdempotencyKey at creation and otherwise only calls Cancel() or Ship(). Checked: git grep -n -e "Items\." -e "Quantity =" stage-2 -- "*.cs".

In OrderTests @ stage-2, only Constructor_NoItems_Throws and Constructor_QuantityBelowOne_Throws deal with item rules, via the constructor; others use NewOrder() (constructor with OneItem(), quantity 2) and call only MarkPaid, Ship or Cancel; no test references Items.
In db/schema.sql @ stage-2, order_items.product_id REFERENCES products (id) and orders.customer_id REFERENCES customers (id); neither order item rule mentions product or customer data.

An aggregate is drawn around the invariants that must hold together, not around foreign keys; a rule spanning several objects holds only if every change to them passes through one place that checks it.

Input validation (the controller checking each request's fields before calling the service) checks one request when it arrives; an invariant must hold for saved data after every change, whichever code path made it.
git show stage-2:DonHang.Tests/Domain/OrderTests.cs prints the file as it is at tag stage-2.

Outside C#, db/schema.sql @ stage-2 declares order_items.quantity CHECK (quantity > 0), loaded by docker-compose.yml, so PostgreSQL refuses to save an order_items row whose quantity is not above 0; nothing in the schema refuses an orders row with no order_items rows.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: db/schema.sql:29; docker-compose.yml:68; PostgreSQL docs: Constraints / Check Constraints
